newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Tribal tension in Indonesia's Irian said cooling.
newsitem.headline: Tribal tension in Indonesia's Irian said cooling.

text.p: Clashes between rival tribal groups around the mining town of Timika in Indonesia's rugged Irian Jaya province has eased as mediators search for a peaceful solution, a local community leader said on Sunday.

"Up to yesterday they was still fighting. There were many injuries but they were not too serious," a leader from the Amungme Community Institute (Lemasa), Tom Beanal, told Reuters from Timika, some 4,000 km (2,500 miles) east of Jakarta.

"This morning there were people to ready to fight but the church and Lemasa intervened to try and create peace. We hope by the day after tomorrow things will have returned to normal," Beanal said speaking by telephone.
Other residents also reported a quietening down after three days of clashes, although police in Timika declined to comment on the latest developments when contacted on Sunday.

Beanal said four people had died and two remained critically injured in the clashes which were sparked by an attempted robbery or extortion on Wednesday between Amungme and Dani tribesmen in the Kwamki Lama district, five km (three miles) north of Timika.
On Sunday the official Antara news agency, quoting military sources, said three people had died in the clashes, although some residents say up to five had been killed.
In January, six people were killed and more than 60 injured when thousands of Amungme and Dani tribesman clashed near Tembagapura after an alleged rape.

PT Freeport Indonesia, operator of one of the world's largest copper and gold mines at Tembagapura, about 45 km (28 miles) north of Timika, is 81.28 percent owned by Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States. Indonesian interests own the balance.
Company officials have said the relatively isolated lowlands clash has not affected operations at the high-altitude mine.
